data.long_meaning: In Arabic, Wasim means 'helper' or 'supporter'. This name carries a strong sense of being a loyal companion and a source of assistance. The name Wasim carries the meaning “Companion, Helper” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Wasim usually hope their child will grow to embody companion, helper and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Wasim belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Companion, Helper.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Wasim total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

historical_references.reference: Wasim was a famous Muslim general in the armies of the Sultanate of Delhi during the late 13th and early 14th centuries. He is best known for his victories over the Mongol invasions led by Möngke Khan in 1290 and 1295.

Wasim was also a key figure in the Deccan sultanate during the late 15th and early 16th centuries. He is remembered for his successful military campaigns against the Vijayanagara Empire and his establishment of the Bidar Sultanate in 1427.
